# Name: Ouch!!!!  (port)
# When the arm bends the wrong way, play the audio clip on Qt's media player
# (async -- does NOT pause Maya) and paint the arm red. color = colour output.
#
# self.audioData is the SINGLE source of truth for playback. The async player is
# (re)built whenever the CONTENT of self.audioData changes -- so it always plays
# whatever is in the buffer, whether that came from the baked clip, a right-click
# "Load media" onto audioData, or a disk (re)load below. There is exactly ONE
# audio buffer: self.audioData (persistent).
#
# audioFile is an OPTIONAL loader: point it at a .wav / .mp3 / ... and that file
# is read INTO self.audioData. self.audioPath is a TEMPORARY session guard (never
# saved) that just remembers which path we have already loaded, so we do not
# re-read the same file from disk every frame.
#
# (Imports + the ouch_* helper functions live in the Init tab.)

# -- keep self.audioData in sync with an optional audioFile -------------------
# Guarded as a whole so a headless / Qt-less session -- or a not-yet-loaded Init
# namespace -- can never stop the colour output below from computing.
try:
    raw = self.audioFile or ""

    # First eval this session: a buffer we already carry (the baked clip, or a
    # right-click load that was saved) is authoritative -- adopt the current
    # audioFile as "already loaded" so a reopened scene never re-reads it from
    # disk and clobbers the buffer. Only a genuinely EMPTY buffer loads on open.
    if not hasattr(self, "audioPath"):
        self.audioPath = raw if getattr(self, "audioData", None) else None

    # Load from disk ONLY when audioFile names a path we have not already loaded
    # this session. Mark the guard even on failure so a bad path can't re-read
    # every frame.
    if raw != self.audioPath:
        self.audioPath = raw
        path = ouch_resolve_clip_path(raw)
        if path:
            data = ouch_load_bytes(path)
            if data is not None:
                self.audioData = data          # the ONE audio buffer (persistent)

    # (Re)build the async player whenever the BUFFER CONTENT changes -- covers a
    # disk reload AND a manual right-click "Load media" onto audioData. Latched
    # on a content hash so a Qt-less session doesn't retry it on every eval.
    data = getattr(self, "audioData", None)
    if data:
        sig = ouch_bytes_signature(data)
        if getattr(self, "_player_sig", None) != sig:
            self._player_sig = sig
            old = getattr(self, "_player", None)
            if old is not None:
                try:
                    old.stop()
                except Exception:
                    pass
            self._player = ouch_make_player(data, sig)
except Exception:
    pass

# -- colour + one-shot playback ----------------------------------------------
# Session-only latch so the bend audio plays once per bend (seeded here so a
# vanilla node -- or one whose Init namespace hasn't loaded -- never reads an
# unset self.pain in the red branch below).
if not hasattr(self, "pain"):
    self.pain = False

self.color = [0, 1, 0]
if self.angle < 0.165009870842:
    self.color = [1, 0, 0]
    if not self.pain:
        self.pain = True
        player = getattr(self, "_player", None)
        if player is not None:
            player.setPosition(0)
            player.play()
else:
    self.pain = False
    # Arm back in a safe position -- stop the clip if it is still playing.
    player = getattr(self, "_player", None)
    if player is not None:
        player.stop()

# --- from module 'mpynode.ui.qt_wrapper' ---
def make_audio_player(path, parent=None):
    """Build an UN-muted QMediaPlayer for a local audio file and return it (or
    None if QtMultimedia is unavailable). The caller keeps the ref and drives
    play() / setPosition(ms) / stop() directly (those are identical across
    PySide2/PySide6). Hides the Qt5/Qt6 source-setting + audio-output split.

    Unlike :func:`start_video_preview` this does NOT mute or loop -- it is for
    the Variables/Watch tab click-to-play / drag-to-scrub waveform audio.

    Returns None when QtMultimedia is unavailable OR a player cannot be
    constructed (e.g. no platform audio backend / device), so callers degrade
    to render-only (waveform shown, no playback) rather than penalize the user.
    """
    if not HAS_QT_MULTIMEDIA:
        return None
    player = None
    try:
        player = QMediaPlayer(parent)
        url = QUrl.fromLocalFile(path)
        if QT_BINDING == "PySide6":
            audio = QAudioOutput()
            audio.setParent(player)  # Qt parent-owns it (GC-safe)
            player.setAudioOutput(audio)
            player.setSource(url)
        else:
            player.setMedia(QMediaContent(url))
            try:
                player.setVolume(100)
            except Exception:
                pass
        return player
    except Exception:
        # A backend failure surfaces AFTER construction, and the player is
        # already parented to a live tab widget, so dropping the Python ref
        # would leak it under the tab. Release it before degrading to None.
        if player is not None:
            try:
                player.deleteLater()
            except Exception:
                pass
        return None

spec.methods:
# Build a complete, self-contained ouch demo: import the bundled skinned arm
# (arm.ma -- a 3-joint chain + skinned mesh), drive `angle` from the elbow's
# rotateY, and shade the arm mesh with a lambert whose colour follows the node's
# `color` output. The node paints RED (and plays the clip) when `angle` drops
# BELOW a small threshold (~9.5 deg), GREEN above it -- so the elbow is keyframed
# through a flex arc: bent (green) -> straightened into NEGATIVE rotateY (red, the
# clip fires) -> bent again (green). Play the timeline to hear the ouch.
#
# The bundled ouch.wav's BYTES are baked PERSISTENTLY onto the node as the
# self.audioData buffer -- the single source of truth for playback -- so the clip
# travels with the scene. The Compute tab (re)builds the async player whenever
# audioData's CONTENT changes, so swapping the clip -- either by pointing
# audioFile at a new file OR by right-clicking audioData and choosing "Load
# media" -- just plays the new sound. audioPath is a temporary runtime guard the
# Compute tab seeds; it is intentionally NOT baked here.
def demo(self):
    from maya import cmds as mc
    import os
    name = self.get_name()
    # --- skinned arm (falls back to a plain chain + cube if missing) --------
    elbow = None
    meshes = []
    try:
        from mpynode._common.util.template_gallery import _bundled_templates_root
        root = _bundled_templates_root()
        arm = os.path.join(root or "", "MPyNode", "Ouch", "arm.ma")
        if os.path.isfile(arm):
            new = mc.file(arm, i=True, ignoreVersion=True,
                          returnNewNodes=True) or []
            joints = mc.ls(new, type="joint", long=True) or []
            # Prefer an exact leaf-name match for the elbow; fall back to a
            # substring (robust to import renames / node-order changes).
            elbow = next(
                (j for j in joints if j.rsplit("|", 1)[-1] == "loarm_r_JNT"),
                None) or next((j for j in joints if "loarm" in j), None)
            meshes = [m for m in (mc.ls(new, type="mesh", long=True) or [])
                      if not mc.getAttr(m + ".intermediateObject")]
    except Exception:
        elbow = None
        meshes = []
    if elbow is None:
        mc.select(clear=True)
        mc.joint(name="ouchShoulder#", position=(0, 0, 0))
        elbow = mc.joint(name="ouchElbow#", position=(3, 0, 0))
        mc.joint(name="ouchWrist#", position=(6, 0, 0))
        geo = mc.polyCube(name="ouchGeo#", width=2, height=2, depth=2)[0]
        mc.setAttr(geo + ".translate", 3.0, 2.0, 0.0, type="double3")
        meshes = mc.listRelatives(geo, shapes=True, fullPath=True) or []
    # Drive `angle` from the elbow's rotateY, then keyframe a flex arc so PLAYING
    # the timeline plays the ouch: the arm starts bent (angle above the red
    # threshold -> GREEN), straightens into NEGATIVE rotateY (angle below the
    # threshold -> RED, the clip fires), then bends back positive (GREEN, silent).
    mc.connectAttr(elbow + ".rotateY", name + ".angle", force=True)
    for f, ry in ((1, 30.0), (45, -30.0), (90, 30.0)):
        mc.setKeyframe(elbow + ".rotateY", time=f, value=ry)
    mc.playbackOptions(min=1, max=90)
    mc.currentTime(1)
    # --- shading -----------------------------------------------------------
    shd = mc.shadingNode("lambert", asShader=True, name="ouchShader#")
    sg = mc.sets(renderable=True, noSurfaceShader=True, empty=True, name=shd + "SG")
    mc.connectAttr(shd + ".outColor", sg + ".surfaceShader", force=True)
    for m in meshes:
        try:
            mc.sets(m, edit=True, forceElement=sg)
        except Exception:
            pass
    mc.connectAttr(name + ".color", shd + ".color", force=True)
    # --- persistent audio --------------------------------------------------
    # Bake the clip's BYTES onto the node as the persistent self.audioData buffer
    # -- the single source of truth for playback, so the demo (and any clip you
    # later drop in via the right-click "Load media" action) travels with the
    # scene. audioFile just points at the source .wav so you can see where the
    # sound came from and re-load it; audioPath / audioSig are NOT baked -- the
    # player now follows audioData's content, not a file signature.
    try:
        from mpynode._common.util.template_gallery import _bundled_templates_root
        root = _bundled_templates_root()
        wav = os.path.join(root or "", "MPyNode", "Ouch", "ouch.wav")
        if os.path.isfile(wav):
            mc.setAttr(name + ".audioFile", wav, type="string")
            with open(wav, "rb") as _fh:
                data = _fh.read()
            self.set_variable("audioData", data, persistent=True)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # This demo IMPORTS arm.ma, so frame the WHOLE scene -- an imported
    # rig can land anywhere, and leaving it off screen shows the user
    # nothing.
    try:
        mc.viewFit(all=True)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return name


@maya_test(label="Ouch: the arm turns red below the pain angle, green above", digits=3)
def test_ouch(self):
    """Same test passes interpreted and compiled (parity): the color output is
    green while the elbow angle is safe and flips red once it bends below the
    ~0.165 rad pain threshold. Drives `self.angle` directly (radians)."""
    from maya import cmds as mc
    from mpynode._common.methods.test_helpers import assert_close
    name = self.get_name()

    def _set(plug, *vals, **kw):
        for s in (mc.listConnections(plug, s=True, d=False, plugs=True) or []):
            mc.disconnectAttr(s, plug)
        mc.setAttr(plug, *vals, **kw)

    prev = mc.currentUnit(query=True, angle=True)
    mc.currentUnit(angle="rad")
    try:
        _set(name + ".angle", 0.5)             # safe (> ~0.165 rad) -> green
        mc.dgdirty(name + ".color")
        green = mc.getAttr(name + ".color")[0]
        assert_close(list(green), [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],
                     msg="arm should be green above the pain angle; got %r" % (green,))

        _set(name + ".angle", 0.05)            # bent the wrong way -> red
        mc.dgdirty(name + ".color")
        red = mc.getAttr(name + ".color")[0]
        assert_close(list(red), [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
                     msg="arm should be red below the pain angle; got %r" % (red,))
    finally:
        mc.currentUnit(angle=prev)
